newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close higher in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close higher in lackluster trade.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended a thinly traded session firmer amid light local and speculative buying, trading sources said.
Prices retraced some of the sharp losses made early in the week in volume estimated at only 2,200 lots compared with Thursday's official 2,794 lots.
Analysts said the market remains weak technically, with support in July pegged at 72.00 cents a lb, followed by an ultimate downside objective of 65.45 cents.

But Merrill Lynch noted in a weekly citrus comment that the fundamental picture is not as negative as may traders believe. The last weekly movement figure reflected strong movement and low imports, while Nielsen data showed a jump in retail sales of orange juice in the latest four-week period, the letter said.
Additionally, the sharp decline in open interest this week reduced the risk of heavy deliveries during the notice period.
There have been no delivery notices issued to date.
The May contract ended 1.40 cents higher at 74.50 cents after trading from 75.50 to 73.25 cents. The rest of the board closed 0.35 to 0.50 firmer.
July closed at a 1.70 premium to May compared with a 2.60 premium on Thursday.
USDA will release its monthly crop report May 12. The last report put Florida's output at 221.2 million 90-lb boxes, in 1996/97. Yields were estimated at 1.57 gallons per box.
The first Brazilian estimate for the 1997/98 crop will be released May 20.
